## Current signals

- WebNR remains a local-first browser reader and may be described as an independent browser-based alternative for some Legado users and web-first reading workflows. It is unaffiliated with Legado and is not an official Legado web client. Arbitrary Legado source JSON is not yet a drop-in WebNR runtime; compatibility claims remain tied to tested capability levels and versioned fixtures.
- Pull request #126 publishes the 2026-08-30 versioned Legado compatibility report and fixture suite `2026-08-30.1`, plus a local-only inspector. L1 import/inspection is implemented; L2 declarative, L3 stateful, L4 script, and L5 Bridge/WebView requirements are recognized but are not executed. Inspection is bounded to 2 MiB and 500 source definitions, preserves unknown top-level fields, and performs no target-site requests, source-rule execution, login, cookie, JavaScript, WebView, CAPTCHA, paywall, robots, DRM, or access-control bypass.
- The 2026-08-30 Legado source program screened five public source-definition/collection families and admitted a clean-room compatibility-corpus integration rather than third-party novel-site ingestion. The three committed synthetic fixtures cover declarative, stateful, and script/Bridge shapes without copying third-party story text, credentials, cookies, or real site rules. Compatibility evidence is not treated as source-admission permission.
- `https://www.webnovel.win/` is the sole canonical public identity for documentation, reader-facing articles, search indexing, canonical tags, sitemap, and RSS. `https://app.webnovel.win/` is the reader application runtime; `https://autoarchive.github.io/webNR/` is an attributable documentation build mirror only.
- Pull request #124 adds `Classics & Open Reading Discovery Starter`, a three-route native source for Lit2Go, Alpheios Texts, and Perseus Scaife Viewer. The source is intentionally bounded to first-party discovery links plus WebNR-authored metadata. It does not crawl, poll, proxy, mirror, download origin media, copy origin catalog/text, create accounts, or bypass authentication, robots, paywalls, rate limits, or access controls.
- Lit2Go is admitted only as discovery because its current first-party reuse terms place educational, non-commercial, and quantity boundaries on reuse. Alpheios Texts states a default CC BY-SA 4.0 license unless otherwise indicated, but WebNR does not yet model item-level exceptions and attribution inheritance for that collection. Scaife Viewer exposes a broad classical-text reading environment, but this audit did not establish one blanket redistribution grant for every edition and translation. Open access or open licensing alone is not treated as proof that WebNR has implemented a safe richer adapter.
- StoryWeaver remains a strong future candidate with first-party CC BY 4.0 policy evidence, but direct reader/open-content requests returned HTTP 402 in the 2026-08-29 verification environment, so reliable reader-path availability was not inferred from indexed policy pages. Project Runeberg remains an item-specific audit candidate because current project notes combine free electronic editions, relaxed copyright caution for some newer material, and explicit server-pressure concerns.
- Pull request #122 publishes the August 2026 `Web Novel Discussion Radar` and adds `Web Novel Discussion Radar Starter`, a seven-route native source spanning Royal Road recommendation/debate routes, Progression Fantasy and LitRPG recommendation threads, a translated-web-fiction recommendation thread, and Scribble Hub discoverability discussion. The source stores only first-party URLs plus WebNR-authored metadata and performs no remote synchronization, API call, credential use, post/comment copying, account automation, crawler/CAPTCHA/robots bypass, or story-text mirroring.
- The Discussion Radar uses a reproducible 2026-08-01 through 2026-08-28 research window and a `五字段需求卡 + 三层发现网络 + 月度快照` synthesis. Its current article contains more than 5,000 Chinese main-text characters, 21 academic/research references, and 27 first-party/platform/community references. Community observations remain dated qualitative evidence rather than population-level metrics.
- `Fanfiction Discovery Starter` remains at eight audited first-party discovery destinations: FanFiction.Net, Fimfiction, Scribble Hub, Archive of Our Own (AO3), SquidgeWorld, fanfiction.lol, Sunset, and Asianfanfics. The shipped capability remains static link-only: WebNR stores destination URLs plus WebNR-authored descriptions/labels and does not crawl, poll, proxy, mirror, download, automate accounts, bypass access controls, or copy origin works, story metadata, covers, ratings, comments, bookmarks, or story text.
- AO3 remains admitted for first-party Work Search discovery. Official canonical-tag Atom feeds remain a richer machine-interface candidate, but WebNR does not yet claim Atom synchronization; runtime transport, stable identity, update semantics, response bounds, cadence, attribution, and versioned fixtures must be proven first.
- Fimfiction remains the strongest official-API upgrade candidate technically, but the 2026-08-27 audit identified a concrete external prerequisite. Current first-party developer documentation uses OAuth2 and current Application Management documentation says a new API application must presently be created by Fimfiction after contacting the site operator. WebNR has no registered Fimfiction application/client identity in the repository, so it must not claim a working API adapter or fabricate credentials. Once an application identity exists, implement bounded OAuth transport, rate-limit/backoff, caching, stable story identity, sparse fields, cursor pagination, response/timeout bounds, provenance, attribution, update/deletion semantics, and versioned fixtures.
- The currently accepted maintained source set is: WebNR Originals, Aozora Bunko Starter, Standard Ebooks Starter, Project Madurai Starter, English Serial Platforms Starter, Project Gutenberg Starter, Global Grey Starter, Online Books Page Starter, Wolne Lektury Starter, Wikisource Starter, English Web-Fiction Discovery Starter, Chinese Web-Fiction Platforms Starter, Japanese Web-Fiction Platforms Starter, Korean Web-Fiction Platforms Starter, Progression & LitRPG Publisher Discovery Starter, Fanfiction Discovery Starter, Web Novel Discussion Radar Starter, and Classics & Open Reading Discovery Starter. Rights/access behavior remains source-specific; several maintained catalogs are intentionally link-only at their current proven capability level.
- The deferred/source-audit queue still includes candidates such as Project Runeberg, StoryWeaver, Baen Free Library, LitFic, Betakyte, Hungry's Hedgerow, Ream, Laterpress, Fanqie / 番茄小说, Changpei / 长佩文学, 潇湘书院, 红袖读书, SF轻小说 / 菠萝包轻小说, 刺猬猫, ハーメルン, Nolaノベル, ノベモア, ノベルアップ＋, pixiv novels, 카카오페이지 / KakaoPage, 조아라 / Joara, OneStory, Bookcube, MrBlue, Ascendant Reads, ProgFans, Royal Guard Publishing, The Legion Publishers, Twisting the Hellmouth, Ad Astra current-primary integration, CFAA, Quotev, and MediaMiner.
